output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
#define working directory
wd = ""
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = paste0(wd, "UKB_Limited/"))
```

## Read in data
```{r}
results <- read.csv("cluster_results_with_labels.csv")
```

## Prepare data in R
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

#convert binary variables to factors
results_df <- results %>%
  mutate(Hypertension = ifelse(Hypertension > 0.5, 1, 0)) %>% 
  mutate(across(
    where(~ all(na.omit(.x) %in% c(0, 1, "0", "1", TRUE, FALSE, "TRUE", "FALSE", "True","False"))),
    ~ factor(
        case_when(
          .x %in% c(1, "1", TRUE, "TRUE", "True")  ~ "Yes",
          .x %in% c(0, "0", FALSE, "FALSE", "False") ~ "No",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_   # keep NA as NA
        ),
        levels = c("No", "Yes")
      )
  )) %>% 
  mutate(Cluster = as.factor(Cluster))

#recode clusters for consistency
results_df$Cluster <- factor(results_df$Cluster,
                             levels = c("3", "1", "2", "4"),
                             labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4"))


table(results_df$Cluster)
```


## Create visualization for continuous variables
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Example: replace with your actual dataframe and variable names
vars_to_plot <- c("DBP", "SBP", "Age", "BMI", "Alcohol", "Income", "Education")

# Convert from wide to long format
df_long <- results_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(vars_to_plot),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Value")

# Create boxplots, faceted in a 2x4 grid
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Cluster, y = Value, fill = Cluster)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, nrow = 2, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Numeric Variables\nAcross Clusters",
    x = "Cluster",
    y = "Value"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  )
ggsave("ContClust.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```
## Create visualizations for categorical variables
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Specify your grouping (factor) variable
factor_var <- "Cluster"  # replace with your grouping variable

#save variables with labels for graph
var_labels <- c(
  Sex_Male = "Male",
  Acute.Myocardial.Infarction = "Acute Myocardial\nInfarction",
  Angina.Pectoris = "Angina Pectoris",
  Atrial.Fibriliation = "Atrial\nFibrillation",
  Blockage = "Blockage",
  Cerebral.Infarction = "Cerebral\nInfarction",
  Chronic.Ischemic.Heart.Disease = "Chronic Ischemic\nHeart Disease",
  Chronic.Rheumatic.Heart.Disease = "Chronic Rheumatic\nHeart Disease",
  Heart.Failure = "Heart Failure",
  Hypertension = "Hypertension",
  Hypotension = "Hypotension",
  Pulmonary.Embolism = "Pulmonary\nEmbolism",
  Diabetes = "Diabetes",
  Alzheimers.Disease = "Alzheimer's\nDisease",
  Father.Alzheimers = "Father\nAlzheimer's",
  Mother.Alzheimers = "Mother\nAlzheimer's",
  beta_blockers = "Beta Blockers",
  calcium_channel_blockers = "Calcium Channel\nBlockers",
  diuretics = "Diuretics",
  statins = "Statins",
  angiotensin_antagonists = "Angiotensin\nAntagonists",
  anticoagulants = "Anticoagulants",
  Smoking_Current = "Current Smoker",
  Smoking_Previous = "Previous Smoker"
)

variable_order <- names(var_labels)
# Automatically detect all factor variables except the grouping variable
factor_vars <- names(results_df)[sapply(results_df, is.factor) & names(results_df) != factor_var]

# Convert from wide to long format
df_long_factors <- results_df %>%
  select(all_of(factor_var), all_of(factor_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(factor_vars),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Value") %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = variable_order))

# Convert factor levels like "Yes"/"No" → logical TRUE/FALSE if applicable
df_long_factors <- df_long_factors %>%
  mutate(Value = Value %in% c("Yes", "TRUE", "True", "1"))

# Compute proportion of "Yes" (TRUE) for each Cluster × Variable
df_prop <- df_long_factors %>%
  group_by(!!sym(factor_var), Variable) %>%
  summarise(Proportion = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Create barplots showing proportion of "Yes" for each variable by Cluster
plot <- ggplot(df_prop, aes(x = !!sym(factor_var), y = Proportion, fill = !!sym(factor_var))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, nrow = 4, ncol = 6,
             labeller = labeller(Variable = var_labels)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Condition\nAcross Clusters",
    x = "Cluster",
    y = "Proportion of 'Yes'"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 20)
  )

plot
ggsave("CategoricalClust.png", width = 12, height = 10)
```

## Add analysis with imaging variables
```{r}
# Read in datafile
allVars <- read.csv(paste0(wd, "Parents_AD/cluster_results_allVars.csv"))

# Perform preprocessing
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

allVars_df <- allVars %>%
  mutate(Hypertension = ifelse(Hypertension > 0.5, 1, 0)) %>% 
  mutate(across(
    where(~ all(na.omit(.x) %in% c(0, 1, "0", "1", TRUE, FALSE, "TRUE", "FALSE", "True", "False"))),
    ~ factor(
      case_when(
        .x %in% c(1, "1", TRUE, "TRUE", "True")  ~ "Yes",
        .x %in% c(0, "0", FALSE, "FALSE", "False") ~ "No",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      levels = c("No", "Yes")
    )
  )) %>% 
  mutate(Cluster = as.factor(Cluster))

table(allVars$Cluster)

# Automatically detect all numeric variables
vars_to_plot <- names(allVars_df)[sapply(allVars_df, is.numeric)]

#save variables with labels for graph
var_labels <- c(
  Age = "Age",
  Education = "Eduction\n(Years)",
  Income = "Annual Household\nIncome (£)",
  Physical.Activity = "Physical Activity\n(Days/Week)",
  Alcohol = "Alcohol\n(Drinks/Year)",
  SBP = "SBP",
  DBP = "DBP",
  BMI = "BMI",
  HDL = "HDL",
  LDL = "LDL",
  brainPC1 = "Brain PC 1",
  brainPC2 = "Brain PC 2",
  brainPC3 = "Brain PC 3",
  brainPC4 = "Brain PC 4",
  cognitivePC1 = "Cognitive PC 1",
  heartPC1 = "Heart PC 1",
  heartPC2 = "Heart PC 2",
  heartPC3 = "Heart PC 3"
)
variable_order <- names(var_labels)

# Convert from wide to long format
df_long <- allVars_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars_to_plot),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = variable_order))

# Create boxplots for all numeric variables
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Cluster, y = Value, fill = Cluster)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, nrow = 6, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = labeller(Variable = var_labels)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Numeric Variables\nAcross Clusters",
    x = "Cluster",
    y = "Value"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  )
ggsave("ContClusterAllVars.png", height = 10, width = 8)
```
